text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar prices in London ended higher after a muted day's trading. By the close front month October was $1.10 higher at $329.00 per tonne. October dominated the volume with 967 of a total 1,861 lots.

Raw sugar futures in New York closed firmer but off the new lifetime highs made across the board amid early mixed buying, traders said. Trade buying on the open carried second position March to a high of 11.90 cents/lb. Benchmark October opened unchanged but broke through its previous high of 11.65 cents/lb and climbed to 11.70 cents/lb on the reopen amid fund buying.

The benchmark October contract settled 0.07 cent higher at 11.63 cents/lb, having ranged from 11.70 to 11.55 cents/lb. March finished up 0.11 at 11.90 cents/lb, just under the lifetime high of 11.91 cents/lb reached just ahead of the close. The rest of the board ended 0.11 to 0.15 cent firmer.

Traders considered the market to act rather constructively given the negative factors such as a huge open interest in the most active October contract, lack of physical offtake, and steady selling by the trade. Some believe that the funds could continue their buying spree if the October contract breaks today's high of 11.70 cents/lb.

ROMANIA - Sugar imports in March 1997 amounted to 19,857 tonnes, raw value, up from 13,776 tonnes imported in March 1996. This brought cumulative imports in September/March 1996/97 up to 181,478 tonnes compared to 77,690 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 327,159 tonnes compared to 275,178 tonnes in 1994/95.

Major countries of origin in 1996/97 were Brazil with 87,499 tonnes whites against 28,000 tonnes, Cuba with 22,785 tonnes compared to nil, Moldova with 22,559 tonnes against 12,976 tonnes and Austria with 16,761 tonnes compared to 9,612 tonnes. Given expectations of an only slightly higher crop in 1997/98 sugar imports can be estimated to stay at around 300,000 tonnes.

SOUTH KOREA - Sugar imports in January 1997 amounted to 183,523 tonnes, raw value, hardly changed from the 188,916 tonnes imported in January 1996. Total imports in 1996 reached 1.399 million tonnes compared to 1.306 million tonnes in 1995. Major countries of origin in January 1997 were Australia with 107,517 tonnes raws against 108,137 tonnes, Thailand with 56,000 tonnes compared to 62,912 tonnes and South Africa with 19,979 tonnes compared to 2,000 tonnes.

Sugar exports in January 1997 reached 36,208 tonnes, down from 44,542 tonnes exported in January 1996. Total exports in 1996 amounted to 300,637 tonnes compared to 247,235 tonnes in 1995. Major countries of destination in January 1997 were Indonesia with 11,400 tonnes whites against 23,200 tonnes, Hong Kong with 15,718 tonnes compared to 9,071 tonnes and Vietnam with 3,000 tonnes against nil.

GREECE - The third beet tests of July 10 show that the beet crop may recover from last year's rather disappointing results. Root weight reached 37.77 tonnes per ha, up from 32.95 tonnes in 1996, but still below the 49.05 tonnes attained in 1995.

Sugar content amounted to 13.08 per cent, up on the 12.83 per cent in 1996 and also above the 12.42 per cent in 1995. This resulted in a sugar weight of 4.94 tonnes per ha, more than 17 per cent up on the 1996 result, but down almost 20 per cent on the level attained in 1995. There are five sugar factories operating in Greece.
